**Test image key features:**
- Pale tan/beige girdling lesion at a branch node junction
- Dry, shrunken stem tissue at the lesion
- Dead, shriveled branch tissue hanging to the right
- Otherwise healthy surrounding green foliage

**Reference comparisons:**
- Alternaria: Dark blackish canker at soil line - color doesn't match
- Alternaria #2: Microscopy only
- Phytophthora Blight: Dark water-soaked blackened stems - doesn't match
- Sclerotinia #1: Widespread wilt pattern - relates to stem girdling outcome

- Southern Blight: White mycelium at soil line - location and pattern don't match
- Bacterial Canker: Leaf yellowing symptoms - doesn't match
- Gray Mold: Fruit lesion - doesn't match

The pale tan/bleached girdling lesion at a node, causing branch die-back above it, is most consistent with **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**. Sclerotinia causes bleached, tan-colored stem lesions that girdle the stem and result in wilting/death of tissue above the lesion - matching all key features of the test image.
